en.title: Xbox Explores Nuclear Exclusivity Strategy, But Is It a Real Threat?
en.summary: A leaked Xbox survey suggests a radical shift towards making nearly all first-party games console exclusive, excluding Call of Duty. This move, if enacted, could dramatically reshape the gaming landscape for PlayStation and Nintendo owners.
en.body:
Microsoft has reportedly sent out a survey to a select group of Xbox Insiders, probing their reactions to a drastic "nuclear option" for game exclusivity. The hypothetical scenario presented is stark: all future Xbox-developed titles, with the notable exception of the **Call of Duty** franchise, would become console exclusives to Xbox platforms. This aggressive strategy would also impact existing titles like **Minecraft**, which would cease to be available on PlayStation or Nintendo consoles and would no longer receive content updates, though players would retain access to purchased content.

This survey comes at a time when Xbox has been strategically releasing some previously exclusive titles onto other platforms, such as **Grounded** and **Hi-Fi Rush**. However, the company has also reaffirmed its commitment to console exclusives, with titles like **Gears of War: E-Day** and **Clockwork Revolution** confirmed as permanent Xbox console exclusives. The survey's questions delve into how users would react, asking whether they would purchase a new Xbox Series X|S, play on PC, or simply skip the games if they were no longer available on their preferred console. It even specifically queries about potential player behavior regarding franchises like **Fallout**.

## The Stakes for Gamers

This potential shift in strategy raises significant questions for the gaming community. For years, the debate between open platforms and strict console exclusivity has been a defining feature of the industry. While some see this survey as a sign of desperation from Xbox to boost hardware sales amidst declining revenue, others view it as a bold, albeit controversial, move to reclaim market share. The inclusion of **Call of Duty** as an exception is particularly telling, given its massive install base across all platforms and Microsoft's significant investment in the franchise. The survey's focus on player migration to PC or new Xbox hardware highlights Microsoft's desire to understand the economic and behavioral impacts of such a monumental decision.

## What's Next

While this survey represents Microsoft's internal research and may not directly translate into a finalized strategy, it offers a fascinating glimpse into the future of Xbox's platform and content approach. The gaming world will be watching closely to see if this "nuclear option" is ever deployed, and how it might influence the competitive landscape. Upcoming releases like **DOOM: The Dark Ages – Revelations** (multiplatform) and **Halo: Campaign Evolved** (multiplatform, including PS5) suggest that a complete shift to exclusivity is not imminent, but the conversation has certainly been ignited.

content_raw: Microsoft is reportedly surveying a subset of Xbox users about changing its plans for exclusive games going forward--possibly in a big way--and that's no surprise given Xbox CEO Asha Sharma has alluded to changes to the exclusivity strategy in the future . At the same time, a survey like this is not necessarily indicative of anything beyond Microsoft conducting research. After all, there is an entire team at Xbox called Xbox Research that ... researches all manner of things, and the results of that research doesn't always lead to changes in the marketplace. Windows Central reports that a new survey was issued to some Xbox Insiders this week, and the site confirmed the survey to be real. The survey asks how members might feel about the totally nuclear option of making all Xbox-developed games except Call of Duty exclusive to Xbox on console. "Imagine it was announced that all future title releases from every Xbox-developed gaming franchise except Call of Duty will be console-exclusive to Xbox," the survey asks. It goes on: "For Minecraft only, existing titles would no longer be available for purchase on PlayStation or Nintendo consoles and would not receive any new content updates. However, there is no impact to any of the existing titles or content you already own. Nothing changes on PC with this announcement." The survey asks respondents to say in this scenario, where they would be most likely to play any of the exclusive content. The choices are: On an existing Xbox I own On a new Xbox Series X|S I would decide to purchase On a PC I would skip playing because it would now be unavailable on my preferred console Something else Not interested in playing the exclusive content Another page of the survey specifically asks about Fallout, polling users about how they would feel if future Fallout games would be console-exclusive to Xbox, and with nothing changing at all on PC. Windows Central reported that the survey also asked these same questions about The Elder Scrolls, Doom, Physint, Diablo, and Minecraft. In a memo to staff, Sharma and Xbox boss Matt Booty said they will “re-evaluate” the approach to exclusivity , which could mean a lot of things. Surveying fans is likely connected to this endeavor. Fans have called on Microsoft to return to exclusive games, but it remains to be seen if that will happen. Sharma and Booty also said they will consider changing things up in regards to “windowing,” which followed on from a report that said some other games beyond Call of Duty titles could be kept out of Game Pass at launch and for a period of time, similar to how movies are only available in theaters at first before coming to digital and streaming. The so-called nuclear option of making all non-Call of Duty first-party games exclusive to Xbox on console would indeed be a bonafide return to exclusivity, but it also seems quite unlikely given how much money Microsoft could miss out on.
